definitions.definition: A device for transmitting conversations and other sounds in real time across distances, now often a small portable unit also capable of running software etc.
To call (someone) using a telephone.
A speech segment that possesses distinct physical or perceptual properties, considered as a physical event without regard to its place in the phonology of a language.
(chiefly British) An area of land; a district, region.

A set region of land having particular human occupation or agreed limits, especially inhabited by members of the same race, speakers of the same language etc., or associated with a given person, occupation, species etc.
The territory of a nation, especially an independent nation state or formerly independent nation; a political entity asserting ultimate authority over a geographical area; a sovereign state.
(usually preceded by “the”) A rural area, as opposed to a town or city; the countryside.
The rock through which a vein runs.
The female genitalia, especially the vagina.
From or in the countryside or connected with it.
Of or connected to country music.
A style of popular music that originated in the folk music of the rural population of the southern and western United States and characterized by string-band instruments and simple melodies.
A wheeled vehicle that moves independently, with at least three wheels, powered mechanically, steered by a driver and mostly for personal transportation.
definitions.example: She drove her car to the mall.

definitions.definition: A wheeled vehicle, drawn by a horse or other animal; a chariot.
An unpowered unit in a railroad train.
definitions.example: The conductor coupled the cars to the locomotive.

definitions.definition: An individual vehicle, powered or unpowered, in a multiple unit.
definitions.example: The 11:10 to London was operated by a 4-car diesel multiple unit.

definitions.definition: A passenger-carrying unit in a subway or elevated train, whether powered or not.
definitions.example: From the frontmost car of the subway, he filmed the progress through the tunnel.

definitions.definition: A rough unit of quantity approximating the amount which would fill a railroad car.
definitions.example: We ordered five hundred cars of gypsum.

definitions.definition: The moving, load-carrying component of an elevator or other cable-drawn transport mechanism.
definitions.example: Fix the car of the express elevator - the door is sticking.

definitions.definition: The passenger-carrying portion of certain amusement park rides, such as Ferris wheels.
definitions.example: The most exciting part of riding a Ferris wheel is when your car goes over the top.

definitions.definition: The part of an airship, such as a balloon or dirigible, which houses the passengers and control apparatus.
A sliding fitting that runs along a track.
The aggregate of desirable characteristics of a car.
definitions.example: Buy now! You can get more car for your money.

definitions.definition: A floating perforated box for living fish.
A turn.
The first part of a cons in LISP. The first element of a list
To change place.
To change in state or status
To move through time.
To be accepted.
In any game, to decline to play in one's turn.
To do or be better.
To take heed.
The period of time that has already happened, in contrast to the present and the future.
definitions.example: a book about a time machine that can transport people back into the past

definitions.definition: (grammar) The past tense.
Having already happened; in the past; finished.
definitions.example: past glories

definitions.definition: (postmodifier) Following expressions of time to indicate how long ago something happened; ago.
Of a period of time: having just gone by; previous.
definitions.example: during the past year

definitions.definition: (grammar) Of a tense, expressing action that has already happened or a previously-existing state.
definitions.example: past tense

definitions.definition: In a direction that passes.
definitions.example: I watched him walk past

definitions.definition: Passing by, especially without stopping or being delayed.
definitions.example: Ignore them, we'll play past them.

definitions.definition: Beyond in place, quantity or time.
definitions.example: count past twenty

definitions.definition: No longer capable of.
definitions.example: I'm past caring what he thinks of me.

definitions.definition: Having recovered or moved on from (a traumatic experience, etc.).
A journey; an excursion or jaunt
definitions.example: We made a trip to the beach.

definitions.definition: A stumble or misstep
definitions.example: He was injured due to a trip down the stairs.

definitions.definition: An error; a failure; a mistake
A period of time in which one experiences drug-induced reverie or hallucinations
definitions.example: He had a strange trip after taking LSD.

definitions.definition: A faux pas, a social error
Intense involvement in or enjoyment of a condition
definitions.example: ego trip; power trip; nostalgia trip; guilt trip

definitions.definition: A mechanical cutout device
A trip-switch or cut-out
definitions.example: It's dark because the trip operated.

definitions.definition: A quick, light step; a lively movement of the feet; a skip
definitions.example: trip the light fantastic W

definitions.definition: A small piece; a morsel; a bit
The act of tripping someone, or causing them to lose their footing
A single board, or tack, in plying, or beating, to windward
To fall over or stumble over an object as a result of striking it with one's foot
definitions.example: Be careful not to trip on the tree roots.

definitions.definition: (sometimes followed by "up") to cause (a person or animal) to fall or stumble by knocking their feet from under them
definitions.example: A pedestrian was able to trip the burglar as he was running away.

definitions.definition: To be guilty of a misstep or mistake; to commit an offence against morality, propriety, etc
To detect in a misstep; to catch; to convict
To activate or set in motion, as in the activation of a trap, explosive, or switch
definitions.example: When we get into the factory, trip the lights.

definitions.definition: To be activated, as by a signal or an event
definitions.example: The alarm system tripped, throwing everyone into a panic.

definitions.definition: To experience a state of reverie or to hallucinate, due to consuming psychoactive drugs
definitions.example: After taking the LSD, I started tripping about fairies and colors.

definitions.definition: To journey, to make a trip
definitions.example: Last summer we tripped to the coast.

definitions.definition: To move with light, quick steps; to walk or move lightly; to skip
To raise (an anchor) from the bottom, by its cable or buoy rope, so that it hangs free
To pull (a yard) into a perpendicular position for lowering it
(most commonly used in the form tripping) to become unreasonably upset, especially over something unimportant; to cause a scene or a disruption
A herd or flock of sheep, goats, etc.
A troop of men; a host
A flock of wigeons
Three of a kind, especially if one of the three cards is in one's hand and the other two are on the board. Compare set.

A way used for travelling between places, originally one wide enough to allow foot passengers and horses to travel, now (US) usually one surfaced with asphalt or concrete and designed to accommodate many vehicles travelling in both directions. In the UK both senses are heard: a country road is the same as a country lane.
A road; or particularly a car, as a means of transportation.
definitions.example: We travelled to the seaside by road.

definitions.definition: A path chosen in life or career.
An underground tunnel in a mine.
A railway or a single railway track.
The act of riding on horseback.
A hostile ride against a particular area; a raid.
(often in the plural) A partly sheltered area of water near a shore in which vessels may ride at anchor; a roadstead.
A journey, or stage of a journey.
A way or route.
At the venue of the opposing team or competitor; on the road.
(Slang) Having attributes, primarily masculine, suggesting a tendency towards minor crime. Usually used by youths endearingly; glorifying crime.
